# Experiment log: every change and its effect

One entry per change to the agent: **what changed, why, the effect on scores, verdict.** Newest at the bottom. All sandbox scores are on `case:D01` (foundry +8.8 %, single supplier, `stabilise`) and `case:D02` (shaft RFQ, 2 suppliers, `leverage`). Sandbox sessions are free; practice sessions cost team quota.

Related: [[Runs/Search-Results|Search results (auto-generated)]] · [[Runs/2026-10-10-sandbox-engine-runs|Sandbox engine runs 1–9]] · [[../App/Engine-Prototype|Engine]] · [[../App/Target-C-Model|Target C model]] · [[../App/Arena-Workflow-and-Learnings|Workflow & learnings]]

## ⭐ Current best (update after every experiment)

| | D01 | D02 | Mean | Settings | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Recommended: algorithm A2** (= A + practice fixes) | **0.979** | **0.626** (0.598, 0.640, 0.640) | **0.803** | A + safe push, bottleneck anchor, say-fixed, meet supplier-introduced terms, RFQ in-flight close guard | E17 |
| Algorithm A (previous) | **0.979** | **0.640** (3/3 runs, stable) | **0.810** | e=2, T=4, anchor −3 % vs our target, **2** term sheets, 2 facts/message, 2 pushes of 1 %, hold if the supplier gave > 0.5 %, no calc; + per-thread RFQ clocks + teammates' guards | E15 |
| **Practice (hosted, 10 cases)** | A: mean **0.557**; best-per-case with the teammate's orchestra: **0.671** | | | P02 0.684 and P04 0.874 are case records; P10 0 (walk-away after our push) | E16 |
| Best single D02 run (not reproducible) | 0.943 | 0.724 | 0.833 | gen-1 best mean (3 sheets); its D02 replay scored 0.535 | Search gen 1 |
| **Best D01** | **0.979** (€49.50, C €409.5k vs c_best €408.6k) | | | + only **2** term sheets per message, no rival disclosure | Search gen 1 |
| Best D02 | | **0.724** (J1 €13.80 FCA 14 d) | | best-mean config, but **D02 is noisy**: the same config replayed 0.535 vs 0.682 | Search gen 1 |
| Previous best (hand-designed) | 0.869 | 0.640 | 0.745–0.755 | run 9 (linear + hold) / run 8 (e=2 + hold) | E9 |

**What works so far (sandbox):** cost-aware package choice (24 months, 14-day payment, 35-day lead time, FCA), conceding visibly every round (linear or early: e = 1–2) instead of holding firm, one or two small asks after a final offer, an extra "hold" round while the supplier still concedes, citing verified data IDs.
**What doesn't:** holding firm until late (Boulware e = 0.2), mirroring the supplier's concessions (reciprocal), small invisible moves, generic arguments without a data ID.

---

## Log

### E0 · Baseline: naive kit agent
- **Change:** none, `arena play` with the kit's naive bot (1 % steps, accepts in round 4).
- **Effect:** practice P01 **0.58**, P07 0.12 (the team's only practice scores, 7.0 on the board); sandbox D01 **0.20**.
- **Verdict:** baseline to beat.

### E1 · Hand negotiation (Claude via scripts)
- **Change:** manual e-mails: 24-month commitment, cited PO IDs, phased start date; D02 parallel threads.
- **Effect:** D01 0.80 → **0.84**; D02 0.22 → **0.33** (2nd run: lead 42 d + EXW + 14 d payment, cited `fc:`/`cost:`/`sc:`).
- **Learned:** a 24-month contract is the biggest single lever in D01 (C −€27k); a quote with missing fields closes on its standard terms (C1's 45-day lead time would break the must-have); each verified fact moves the price once; generic claims without an ID harden the supplier. Details: [[../App/Arena-Workflow-and-Learnings]].

### E2 · Deterministic target C (our own C_best)
- **Change:** `proto/target.py`: for every lever combination, solve the price where the supplier's cash value = its estimated floor, cost it with the published C, take the minimum. Floors come from in-game evidence only.
- **Effect (estimator accuracy):** D01 €397.8k vs true €408.6k (−2.7 %); D02 after round-1 documents €155.9k vs €156.7k (**−0.5 %**).
- **Verdict:** ✅ accurate enough to anchor and to know how far we are from the best. Details: [[../App/Target-C-Model]].

### E3 · Engine v1: research playbook (run 1)
- **Change:** code picks numbers, 3 equal-C term sheets (MESO), Boulware e=0.2 over T=6, one fact per round, AC_next acceptance, RFQ coordinator.
- **Effect:** D01 **0.845** (≈ hand), D02 **0.408** (hand 0.33).
- **Verdict:** ✅ code-chosen packages beat hand play on D02 (35-day lead, FCA).

### E4 · Answer questions, prove rival offer, attach own calc, push after final (run 2)
- **Change:** answer "which volume?", cite the rival's **term-sheet ID** + attach it, attach our calculation (from that supplier's own breakdown), one 1.5 % ask after a final offer (RFQ only).
- **Effect:** D01 0.845 → 0.829 (−0.016, start date fell to Dec), D02 0.408 → **0.429**.
- **Learned:** rival offer IDs are **verified** by the arena (C1 15.70 → 15.30); a push after final got "to get this signed today, 15.20" without a walk-away.

### E5 · Linear concession, T=4 (run 3)
- **Change:** e = 0.2 → **1.0**, T = 6 → 4; push after final in both cases.
- **Effect:** D01 → **0.869**, D02 → **0.556** (+0.13). No supplier went to `final_offer`.
- **Learned:** ❗ **only the supplier's first term sheet can be accepted**; an alternative (`…-a`) returns `422 not a standing offer`. Send its terms back → `agreed` → accept.
- **Verdict:** ✅ big win: suppliers need to see us move.

### E6 · Automate "mirror the alternative sheet" (run 4)
- **Change:** `close()` sends an alternative sheet back before accepting.
- **Effect:** identical to E5 (0.869 / 0.556) **to the cent** → sandbox looked deterministic.

### E7 · Concede early: e = 2 (run 5)
- **Effect:** D01 0.869 → 0.849 (−0.02), D02 0.556 → **0.619** (+0.06).
- **Verdict:** ⚖️ case-dependent: RFQ likes early concession, the single foundry slightly prefers linear.

### E8 · Reciprocal concession (runs 6, 7)
- **Change:** concede α × the supplier's last concession (α = 0.5 / 1.0).
- **Effect:** α=0.5: 0.823 / 0.513; α=1.0: **0.656** / 0.534.
- **Verdict:** ❌ worse. α=1 copied the supplier's big round-0 jump (mostly the structural 24-month switch) and the supplier agreed at a bad price; α=0.5 made our moves too small and J1 went final. **Removed from the engine.**

### E9 · "Hold" round (runs 8, 9)
- **Change:** when the acceptance rule fires but the supplier conceded > 1 % last round and is still open, play one more round at an unchanged goal.
- **Effect:** e=2+hold: 0.849 / **0.640**; linear+hold: **0.869** / 0.619 (D02 +0.02 to +0.06, D01 unchanged).
- **Verdict:** ✅ keep.

### E10 · Refactor: every tactic becomes a `Config` field
- **Change:** `proto/engine.py` rewritten so 16 settings can vary per session (curve, rounds, anchor, holds, pushes, MESO size, package pick, facts per message, rival disclosure, calc, volume answer, tone).
- **Effect:** regression test with the default config = run 9: **0.869 / 0.619, identical**. ✅

### E11 · Bug: unreachable goal accepted the opening quote
- **Found by the search:** with `anchor = −3 %` the D01 goal fell below anything a package can reach (the supplier-health term), no package was generated, and the engine **accepted the opening quote (score 0.0)**.
- **Fix 1:** offer the cheapest feasible package → still chose a **12-month** package (worst for us): 0.37.
- **Fix 2:** among unreachable packages take the lowest-C ones → **0.749** for that weak config. ✅
- **Side incident:** stopping the first search attempt left 6 of our sessions open; the cleanup also walked away from **2 teammate sandbox sessions** (`532aad7996b2fa5c`, `a4b04cf6ba39df77`). Fix: the search now records `opened.txt` / `closed.txt` and `proto/cleanup.py` only touches its own sessions; workers reduced 10 → 4 to leave teammates 6 of the key's 10 slots.

### E12 · Evolutionary tactic search (running)
- **Change:** `proto/search.py`: 24 configs per generation (seeds: run 8, run 9 + 22 random), keep best mean + best per case, breed 20 mutations/crossovers, max 5 generations, stop at mean ≥ 0.90. One control replay per generation checks determinism.
- **Gen 0 done (48 sessions, 24 configs):** best mean **0.812** (D01 **0.943**, D02 **0.682**). Common to the top configs: e = 2, anchor −3 %, 2 pushes of 1 %, no calc attachment. Full tables: [[Runs/Search-Results]].
- **Gen 1 done (stopped by plan after gen 1; 92 sessions, 46 configs in total):** best mean **0.833** (D01 0.943, D02 0.724); best D01 **0.979**, i.e. €49.50 vs the true best package, 0.2 % above c_best.
- **Determinism controls (replay of gen 0's best):** D01 **0.9425 → 0.9425, identical** ✅. D02 **0.682 → 0.535** ⚠️. The single-supplier case is deterministic; the **RFQ case is not** (supplier randomness and/or the timeouts in E14). D02 rankings from single runs are unreliable: a config needs ~3 replays to be judged on D02.
- **Setting effects (mean score per value, gen 0+1; random configs vary several settings at once, so these are hints):**

| Setting | Best value | D01 effect | D02 effect | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Curve end `toward` | **standing offer** | 0.855 vs 0.636 (open quote) | 0.550 vs 0.525 | Concede toward their *current* offer, not the opening quote |
| Rounds `T` | **4** | 0.879 (others 0.59–0.73) | ≈ flat | 4 planned rounds |
| Curve `e` | **2** (concede early) | 0.847 (others 0.63–0.79) | ≈ flat | Visible early movement |
| `anchor` | **−3 %** | 0.861 vs 0.752 (0) vs 0.562 (+6 %) | ≈ flat | Open slightly beyond our target |
| `push` after final | **all** | 0.849 vs 0.753 (off) | 0.570 vs 0.438 (off) | Always ask once more after a final offer |
| `push_pct` | **1 %** | 0.834 vs 0.665 (1.5 %) | ≈ flat | Small asks |
| Term sheets `meso_n` | **2** | 0.872 vs 0.825 (3) vs 0.612 (1) | **0.654** vs 0.484 (3) vs 0.517 (1) | **2 packages beat 3** on both cases |
| `tone` | **warm** | 0.834 vs 0.744 (brief) | 0.563 vs 0.519 | Research finding confirmed: warmth helps |
| `facts` per message | 2 | 0.823 vs 0.763 | ≈ flat | slightly better |
| `calc` attachment | off | 0.841 vs 0.718 | ≈ flat | probably confounded (D01 never gets a breakdown) |
| `rival`, `volume`, `pick`, `holds`, `pushes` | – | small | small | no clear effect |

- **⚠️ Earlier determinism question (resolved above):** the default config (run 9) scored D02 **0.597** in the search vs **0.619** twice before. Either the suppliers are not fully deterministic (the API docs say "identical messages need not get identical replies") or load or timing matters. The control replays will tell; until then treat differences < ~0.03 on D02 as noise.

### E13 · Practice adapter (built, not yet played)
- **Change:** `proto/practice.py`: same engine, but facts and floors from the real data package: notice period (letter `doc:` vs contract `ctr:`), should-cost `cost:`, cost-driver index moves `idx:`, order history `po:`, weak scorecards `sc:`, growing forecasts `fc:`, and our alternative quote **only if it is cheaper than the supplier's ask**. Floors: should-cost (supplier plant cost, no margin) → else current price adjusted by driver drift. Supplier cash rate from its credit index.
- **Dry run (no quota):** sensible facts for all 10 hosted cases, e.g. P01: "letter gives 51 days' notice, contract requires 90", should-cost €132.64, electricity −3.7 %, on-time delivery 85.2 %.
- **Next:** play the best search configs on practice cases (costs quota; the team decides how many).

### E14 · RFQ timeouts → per-thread clocks (built, not yet tested)
- **Found in gen 1:** 3 D02 sessions scored **0.0** without a bad tactic: 2 × `session has ended: timeout`, 1 × J1 `walked_away` followed by an accept on the dead thread.
- **Cause:** the 60-second limit runs **per thread from that supplier's reply**. The engine messaged both suppliers and waited for **both** replies before the next round. Under load replies took up to **181 s** (median 24 s), so the fast supplier's clock ran out while we waited for the slow one. Idle time counts as timeouts, and 3 in a row end the thread or session. Sessions had run 4.3–4.5 min.
- **Why it matters for the final:** waves run up to 10 cases in parallel with 2–3 suppliers each, so slow replies will be common, and this would silently lose RFQ deals.
- **Fix (`run_rfq` in `proto/engine.py`):** one worker per supplier thread answers its supplier as soon as it replies (shared target/goal/best offer under a lock, central acceptance). A thread resting on a final offer is pushed or accepted after 90 s idle instead of dying. After any 409 the engine re-reads the thread from the arena (`resync`), and a failed accept falls back to the next-best offer. The single-supplier loop is unchanged (D01 results stay comparable). Backup of the previous engine: `proto/engine_v2_backup.py`.
- **Next:** test on D02 (3–5 replays, since D02 is noisy) and compare score and zero-rate against gen 1.

### E15 · Teammates' findings → guards + 5 named algorithms (running)
- **Read:** Whem's orchestra agent notes and 30 hosted practice sessions (board 28.8 → **60.1, #2**) and Aniket's consolidated findings. Full comparison: [[Teammate-Findings-Comparison]].
- **Agreement:** 4 rounds, visible concessions from round 1, curve aimed at their current offer, one fresh fact per round, per-thread RFQ workers. They reached all of these independently on real suppliers.
- **Always-on fixes taken over:** never offer above the supplier's own offer (their P02 zero); should-cost capped so the opening keeps a sustainable margin (P05/P02); close before the wave cap with `max(90 s, slowest round + 15 s)`.
- **Variants:** A = search best (+2 sheets); B = A + opening-based goal anchors; C = A + RFQ "agreement is the bar" + hold e-mail; D = all teammate ideas; E = A + long contract + say-fixed (practice-only levers).
- **Test:** sandbox D01 × 1 (deterministic) and D02 × 3 (noisy) per variant, 16 sessions.
- **Result:** **A 0.979 / 0.640** (mean 0.810) · B 0.609 / 0.577 · C 0.979 / 0.626 · D 0.609 / 0.584. The opening-based anchors (B, D) open softer than our target (D01 first ask €51.3 vs €47.6) and the deal lands near the first ask (€51.50 vs €49.50). RFQ bar / hold e-mail (C): no gain with 2 suppliers. **Verdict: keep A; keep the teammates' guards; drop opening anchors; test E (long contract + say-fixed) on practice.** Details: [[Teammate-Findings-Comparison]].
- **E14 verified:** 12 D02 sessions with per-thread clocks: **0 timeouts, 0 zeros**; A scored 0.640 three times in a row.

### E16 · Algorithm A on the 10 hosted practice cases (running)
- **Smoke test first (offline, no quota):** the practice adapter on all 10 hosted cases with simulated opening quotes. No crash, every package within the must-haves, 2 packages per case, 3–6 data-backed facts per supplier. The should-cost cap fired on P01 (132.64 → 130.21) and P02 (374.95 → 367.38): the teammates' P02 trap is avoided.
- **Run:** algorithm A × 10 hosted cases, 10 practice sessions (quota 159 → 149), 4 in parallel. Full table: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A]].
- **Result: mean 0.557** (teammate's orchestra best-per-case: 0.602). **5 cases above the teammate's best:** P01 0.801 (0.76), **P02 0.684** (0.18, new case record), P03 0.866 (0.83), **P04 0.874** (0.86, new record, beats Tacto's house agent 0.860), P05 0.510 (0.41). P07 equal (0.699 vs 0.70). **Worse:** P08 0.474 (0.52), P11 0.378 (0.71), P18 0.286 (0.39), **P10 0.000** (0.66).
- **Why the weak cases lost (from the logs):**
  1. **P10 (capacity, bottleneck, no alternative) = 0:** first ask €26.31, 17 % below the €31.68 opening (from should-cost €24.31). The supplier: "Your offer is far below any calculation we can make" → **final offer €33.70, above its own opening**. Then our push after final → it **walked away** → no deal. ❗ Pushing after a final offer is **not** safe on real suppliers (it was in the sandbox), and a bottleneck supplier must not be anchored far below its opening. The teammate anchored 2.4 % below and got 0.66.
  2. **Index facts that backfire (P10, P11, P18):** we cited cost drivers that *rose less than the ask*. Suppliers read them as "Your figures confirm our case: that driver rose." Only falling indices help.
  3. **P11 (quality):** the supplier asked for faster payment every round ("we need faster payment terms"), but payment is fixed in this case, and A doesn't say so (say-fixed is off in A). It stalled at €47.50.
  4. **P18 / P08 (raw material):** both suppliers insist on the AS-14404 **index clause** ("fixed prices over this duration are not possible"). All our packages had no clause, so we never met them on it and accepted their clause terms at the end.
- **Fixes → algorithm A2 (next):** (a) push after a final offer **only** when a rival or alternative backs us up; (b) bottleneck / no-alternative cases: anchor at max(target, opening × 0.97); (c) cite only **falling** index moves; (d) say-fixed on; (e) include the supplier's own index clause in one package when it asks for one.

### E17 · Algorithm A2: fixes for every weakness from practice run A (sandbox retest running)
- **Findings note pushed:** [[Practice-Run-A-Findings]] (vault commit `2ffef7a`).
- **Fixes (config `A2` in `proto/variants.py`):**
  1. **Safe push** (`push="rfq"`): a small ask after a final offer only when another supplier's standing offer backs us up. Never in single-supplier cases (P10 walked away).
  2. **Bottleneck anchor** (`bottleneck_anchor=0.03`): in `secure_supply` cases the first ask is at least opening × 0.97. P10's first ask goes €26.31 → €30.73.
  3. **Only falling indices are cited** (practice adapter): a driver that rose "confirms their case".
  4. **Say-fixed** on: a request about a fixed term is answered (P11 payment).
  5. **Meet fields** (`meet_fields=True`): if the supplier's offer sets a term our packages don't (e.g. its index clause), one package takes its value at equal cost to us, at most one field per message, never more than 15 % below its price. In the smoke test P08/P18 now get "AS-14404 clause, deadband 5 %, €5.23 / €5.67".

(The orchestra has the same rule: "a thread with a message in flight is never accepted".) A first version also parked the best thread and slowed the shared goal to the slowest thread: J1 then stopped at €14.50 instead of €14.20 (D02 0.577). Reverted to own clocks; only *closing* waits.
  2. **Meet-fields chased echoes (D01 0.909):** the foundry's "new" terms were our own packages echoed back, plus its 12-month standard. **Fix:** meet only a term the supplier introduced (never in our sheets), kept in its last two offers, after it has seen ours.

# Teammates' findings vs. our engine

Sources read (2026-10-10, ~15:45): [[../Team-Knowledge/Plan/Review 2026-10-10 - where the points are|Review: where the points are]], [[../Team-Knowledge/Plan/Report 2026-10-10 - profile hook and practice A-B|Report: profile hook and practice A/B]], [[../Team-Knowledge/Playbook/Practice learnings|Practice learnings]], [[../Team-Knowledge/Playbook/Cost levers|Cost levers]], [[../Team-Knowledge/Playbook/Rules of engagement|Rules of engagement]], Decisions [[../Team-Knowledge/Decisions/0002 Orchestra agent|0002]]–[[../Team-Knowledge/Decisions/0005 Writer model|0005]], [[../App/Negotiation-Arena-Full-Findings|Consolidated findings]].
Their agent: the "orchestra" (repo `WhemDev/ehl-tacto`, branch `arda`). **Practice board 60.1, #2, 10/10 deals** after 30 practice sessions. Ours: [[../App/Engine-Prototype|engine]] + [[Experiment-Log|experiment log]].

## Where we agree (independent confirmation)

| Finding | Theirs (hosted practice) | Ours (sandbox search) |
|---|---|---|
| Plan ~4 rounds, suppliers end fast | final or agreement after 2–4 of our messages | T=4 best (0.879 vs 0.59–0.73 on D01) |
| Concede visibly from round 1 | "As your proposed price remains unchanged, we must maintain our offer" | Boulware e=0.2 lost; e=2 best |
| Aim the curve at their *current* offer | fix #7 (P11) | `toward=standing` 0.855 vs 0.636 (D01) |
| One new verified fact per round | "Since you didn't bring any new data…" | each fact moves a price once; repeats are `duplicate` |
| Per-thread workers in RFQ | Decision 0002 (D02 timeout) | E14 (3 zeros in gen 1, same cause) |
| Writer wording barely matters | every writer incl. template within 0.03 | warm > brief by 0.05–0.09 in our search (they test LLM vs template, we test tone) |
| Profiles / supplier archetypes | 58.0 vs 56.8: no measurable gain | not built |

## New to us → implemented

| Idea (their evidence) | Where in our code | Always on / variant |
|---|---|---|
| **Never offer above their offer** (P02: a sheet above the quote was agreed → 0) | `meso()` drops sheets with price > their price or C ≥ C(their offer) | ✅ always on |
| **Should-cost is a weak prior** (P05: above all 3 openings; P02: above the quote) | `practice.py`: floor capped at opening / (1 + sustainable margin) | ✅ always on |
| **Close before the wave cap** with `max(90 s, slowest round + 15 s)` | `near_cap()` / `closing_move()`, `play(..., deadline=)` | ✅ always on when a deadline is passed |
| **Opening-based goal anchors** (routine 12 %, leverage 16 %, quality 10 % below the opening; "the deal lands near our first ask") | `Config.anchor_mode="opening"` | variant **B**, **D** |
| **RFQ: early `agreed` is the bar, not the deal** (P05 0.29 → 0.41) | `Config.rfq_bar` | variant **C**, **D** |
| **Hold e-mail** to a final-offer supplier while rivals move | `Config.rfq_hold` | variant **C**, **D** |
| **Longest contract term where it is free** (P03, P07: "the 36-month contract … allows us to improve our offer") | `Config.long_contract` | variant **D**, **E** (practice only: sandbox has no such option) |
| **Say what is fixed** (P11 asked for faster payment every round; payment was fixed) | `Config.say_fixed` | variant **D**, **E** |
| **Bigger claims pool: `news:` rows** | `Config.news` (practice data) | variant **D** |

Not taken over: supplier **profiles** (no measurable gain in their A/B), the **persona simulator** (not built yet on their side either), the **LLM writer** (no score effect in their race; our templates stay as the fallback).

## The named algorithms

| | Name | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Search best | e=2, T=4, anchor −3 % (vs our target), 2 term sheets, 2 facts/message, 2 pushes of 1 %, hold if the supplier gave > 0.5 %, no calc |
| **B** | A + opening anchors | A, but the first ask = max(our target, opening × (1 − goal %)) |
| **C** | A + RFQ bar & hold e-mail | A + `rfq_bar` + `rfq_hold` |
| **D** | A + all teammate ideas | B + C + long contract + say fixed + news |
| **E** | A + practice levers | A + long contract + say fixed (only visible on practice cases) |

## Results (sandbox, 16 sessions, 2026-10-10 ~16:30)

D01 played once per variant (deterministic), D02 three times (noisy).

| | Algorithm | D01 | D02 (3 runs) | Mean | Deal D01 / D02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Search best** | **0.979** | **0.640** (0.640, 0.640, 0.640) | **0.810** | €49.50 / J1 €14.20 FCA |
| B | A + opening anchors | 0.609 | 0.577 (0.577 ×3) | 0.593 | €51.50 / €14.50 |
| C | A + RFQ bar & hold e-mail | 0.979 | 0.626 (0.640, 0.598, 0.640) | 0.803 | €49.50 / €14.20–14.40 |
| D | A + all teammate ideas | 0.609 | 0.584 (0.577, 0.577, 0.598) | 0.596 | €51.50 / €14.40–14.50 |

**Why B and D lose:** their first ask is **softer** than ours. On D01, A opened at €47.55–47.86 (our computed target), B at €51.31–51.62 (6 % below the opening, the teammates' stabilise anchor). The deal landed near the first ask in both cases: €49.50 vs €51.50. That is exactly the teammates' own lesson ("the deal lands near our first ask"), and the target model gives a bolder first ask than their fixed goal percentages.
**C (RFQ bar + hold e-mail):** no gain on D02 (one run worse). With only two suppliers the bar rarely triggers. Keep it off by default and retest on a 3-supplier RFQ (P05) when quota allows.
**Also confirmed:** the per-thread RFQ fix (E14) works: **12 D02 sessions, 0 timeouts, 0 zeros**, and A scored 0.640 three times in a row (D02 was noisy before the fix).

## Recommendation
- **Main algorithm: A.**
- **Take over from the teammates:** the three always-on guards (never above their offer, should-cost capped, close before the wave cap). They matter on practice and hidden cases, not in the sandbox.
- **Don't take over:** opening-percentage anchors (B). Their *insight* (first ask = deal) holds, but our target-based anchor already uses it better.
- **Still to test on practice (costs quota):** E = A + longest free contract term + say-fixed. Those levers only exist in the practice cases, where the teammates saw suppliers reward them (P03, P07, P11).

def meso(case, sup, target_c, theirs, protect=(), probe=0, gives=None):
    """Up to three term sheets that each cost us `target_c` and differ in the levers: our ideal
    levers, ours except the fields the supplier protects, and the supplier's own levers.
    `sup` is the supplier's entry of `analyse()`; `theirs` its standing terms. `gives` {field: value}:
    trades its profile says it values; then the 2nd sheet offers the first, the 3rd all of them."""
    fields, std, est = lever_fields(case), sup["standard"], None  # plain C; sup["min_price"] is the floor
    ours = sup["ideal_levers"]
    theirs = {**std, **(theirs or {})}
    lo = (est or {}).get("full_cost", 0) * 0.85
    hi = max(sup.get("price") or 0, lo * 1.5)
    # only small trades vary: a lever whose move to the supplier's value is worth at most 4 % of the
    # price (payment days, a date, lead time) - not coverage (contract months, volume), which would
    # need an absurd price to stay equal in C
    ref = complete_offer(case, {**ours, "unit_price": sup.get("anchor_price") or sup.get("price") or 1.0})
    per_unit = cost(case, {**ref, "unit_price": ref["unit_price"] + 1}, std) - cost(case, ref, std)

    def small(f, v):
        t = {**ref, f: snap(case, f, v)}
        return (
            v is not None
            and v != ours.get(f)
            and per_unit > 0
            and must_haves_ok(case, t, std)
            and abs(cost(case, t, std) - cost(case, ref, std)) / per_unit <= 0.04 * ref["unit_price"]
        )

    tradeable = [f for f in fields if small(f, theirs.get(f))]
    held = {f: theirs[f] for f in protect if f in tradeable}
    offered = {f: v for f, v in (gives or {}).items() if f in fields and small(f, v)}
    if offered:  # the profile says what it values: our ideal, then its first trade, then all of them
        first = dict([next(iter(offered.items()))])
        mixes = [ours, {**ours, **held, **first}, {**ours, **held, **offered}]
    else:  # without known trades, each round probes a different lever (round r gives field r)
        keep = list(held) or (tradeable[probe % len(tradeable) :][:1] if tradeable else [])
        mixes = [ours, {**ours, **{f: theirs[f] for f in keep}}, {**ours, **{f: theirs[f] for f in tradeable}}]
    sheets = []
    for levers in mixes:
        levers = {f: snap(case, f, v) for f, v in levers.items() if f in fields}
        price = solve_price(case, levers, std, target_c, est, lo, hi)
        if not price or price <= 0:
            continue
        if sup.get("min_price") and price < sup["min_price"]:  # below the supplier's floor
            price = sup["min_price"]
        t = complete_offer(case, {**levers, "unit_price": price})
        if must_haves_ok(case, t, std) and t not in sheets:
            sheets.append(t)
    return sheets[:3]

# Target C model: computing our own "C_best" deterministically

The arena scores a deal by `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. `C_best` is hidden during a case, so the agent needs its **own estimate of C_best** to know where to anchor and when it is close enough. This note explains how we compute it, and how accurate it was in the sandbox.

Related: [[Engine-Prototype]] · [[Arena-Workflow-and-Learnings]] · [[Research-Negotiation-Techniques]] · [[../Progress/Runs/2026-10-10-sandbox-engine-runs|Sandbox engine runs]]
Code: `~/Documents/EHL-Hackathon-code/starter-kit/proto/target.py`

## The idea

The brief defines `C_best` as *the best package any supplier would ever accept, with every valid lever applied*. A supplier never sells below its **cost floor**. The kit already contains the function that turns any package into the **cash the supplier really receives per unit**: `arena_kit.cost.supplier_value()`. It accounts for payment days (at the supplier's cost of money), the start date (units

So, once we have an estimate of the supplier's floor:

```
for every lever combination allowed by the case (term_options: payment, contract, start date, lead time, Incoterm):
    p*  = the unit price where supplier_value(package at p*) == floor      (bisection)
    C*  = total_cost(package at p*)                                         (the published C)
    skip packages that break a must-have
    strategic goals (stabilise / secure_supply): also try prices above p*, because squeezing
    the supplier below its sustainable margin adds a relationship cost to C
C_target = min over all packages and all suppliers, and our alternative (if any)
```

Two refinements we needed:
- **Lead times faster than the supplier's standard and our need are excluded.** They gain us nothing (C only charges days *beyond* our need) but cost the supplier overtime, which `supplier_value` does not see.
- **Price for a given C (for equal-C term sheets).** With a relationship term, C is *not* monotone in price: it first falls (we stop squeezing) and then rises. `price_for_c` finds the cheapest price by ternary search and solves only on the rising side.

## Estimating the floor from in-game evidence (no hindsight)

| Situation | Estimate | Source in the case |
|---|---|---|
| Price increase, strategic goal (D01) | `full_cost = current_price / (1 + sustainable_margin) × (1 + Σ share × index move)`: the supplier was healthy at today's price, and its cost moved only by the drivers it cites | Case file (`current_unit_price`, `sustainable_margin_pct`) + supplier letter ("WAGES-METAL rose 3.1 % … is 28 % of our cost") |
| Supplier sent a cost breakdown (D02, J1) | `floor = material + wages + conversion` (excluding overhead and profit) | The cost-breakdown XLSX, which you get by asking in round 1 |
| Supplier states its material share (D02, C1) | `floor = material €/unit (from another supplier's breakdown) / material share` | "Material accounts for about 45 % of our cost" |
| Nothing yet | `floor = 85 % of the lowest opening price` | Opening quotes |

The estimate is recomputed after round 1, once the documents have arrived.

## How accurate was it?

After each sandbox case the result reveals the true `c_best`, so we can grade the estimator:

| Case | Our C_target | True c_best | Error | Implied floor (back-solved) | Our floor estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 (foundry, +8.8 %) | €397,779 | €408,624 | **−2.7 %** (too aggressive) | full cost ≈ €48.0 | €47.14 |
| D02 prior (before documents) | €168,427 | €156,739 | +7.5 % (too soft) | n/a | 85 % of €16.00 = €13.60 |
| D02 after round-1 documents | €155,933 | €156,739 | **−0.5 %** | ≈ €12.4–12.5 | C1: 5.56 / 0.45 = **€12.36** |

The best packages implied by the model:
- **D01:** 24 months, start delayed to Feb–Apr 2027, 30 days payment, price about €47.6–49.1. The supplier is left a little below its 4 % margin.
- **D02:** the Polish supplier (C1), 14 days payment, 35 days lead time, DAP or FCA, about €12.8.

## Limits and open questions

- The D01 estimate assumes the supplier earned exactly the sustainable margin at the old price. The truth was about 2 % higher. A better prior might use the price history (`price_conditions`) or a should-cost (`cost:` IDs) when one exists.
- We guessed each supplier's cost of money from its persona (cash-short job shop 20 %, family foundry 10 %, growing exporter 12 %). In the cases we checked, `C_target` was barely sensitive to this.
- The model knows nothing about a supplier's **behaviour**, only its economics. Knowing the target precisely did **not** by itself get us there. See [[Engine-Prototype]] and the runs note for what actually moved suppliers.
- Hosted practice cases have real data packages (`should_cost`, `cost_drivers`, index series), so the floor can be estimated much better there. Port the estimator to use `cost:` and `idx:` data.

# proto: Tugra's buyer engine (branch `tugra`)

A deterministic negotiation engine: **code picks every number, templates write the e-mail** (no LLM needed). It plays
any case of the arena (sandbox, practice, final). The tactics were found by an evolutionary search on the sandbox,
checked on all 10 hosted practice cases, and improved with ideas from the orchestra and a teammate's D02 replay.

Full write-up in the shared Obsidian vault (RxV00/EHL-Hackathon): `Progress/Experiment-Log.md` (every change and its
measured effect), `App/Engine-Prototype.md` (architecture + changelog), `App/Target-C-Model.md`,
`Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings.md`, `Progress/Teammate-Findings-Comparison.md`.

## Results

| Algorithm | D01 (sandbox) | D02 (sandbox, mean of 3) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| naive kit agent | 0.20 | – | |
| A (search winner) | 0.979 | 0.640 | practice: mean 0.557 over 10 cases; P02 0.684 and P04 0.874 were case records |
| A2 (+ fixes from practice) | 0.979 | 0.626 | safe push, bottleneck anchor, say-fixed, meet supplier terms, RFQ in-flight guard |
| **A3 (+ staggered RFQ opening)** | **0.979** | **0.728** (0.740, 0.740, 0.703) | **main algorithm**; the D02 friend replay scored 0.661 |

## Run

From `starter-kit/` (keys in the root `.env`, as in the rest of the repo; `load_env()` reads `.env` in the working
directory, so copy or symlink it if needed):

```bash
# sandbox (free): A3 once on D01, three times on D02 (D02 is noisy)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --cases case:D01:1 case:D02:3 --variants A3

# hosted practice (COSTS QUOTA - ask the team first): facts and floors from the data package
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --practice --cases case:P05:1 --variants A3

# one case, any Config as JSON
ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2, "T": 4, "rfq_stagger": true}' PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D02

# negotiate by hand (interactive)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/chat.py case:D01

# after a kill: close only the sessions this engine opened (never teammates' sessions)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/cleanup.py proto/runs/variants
```

## How A3 negotiates

1. **Target C** (`target.py`): for every allowed combination of levers, the price where the supplier's cash value
   (`cost.supplier_value`) equals its estimated cost floor, costed with the published C; the minimum is our own
   C_best estimate. Floors come from in-game evidence: should-cost (capped so the opening keeps a sustainable
   margin), the supplier's cost breakdown, cost drivers × index moves.
2. **First ask:** 3 % beyond that target; for `secure_supply` (bottleneck) at most 3 % below the opening.
3. **Every message:** 2 term sheets of equal cost to us that differ in the levers the supplier values; 2 new
   verified facts (only *falling* indices); answers to its questions (volume, fixed terms); in an RFQ the best
   rival offer by ID; warm tone. If it keeps insisting on a term we never offered (e.g. its index clause), one
   sheet takes that term at equal cost to us.
4. **Concession:** visible from round 1 (curve e=2), planned over 4 rounds, aimed at its current offer.
5. **RFQ:** one worker per supplier, each on its own 60-second clock; **staggered opening**: the cheapest quote
   first, the others opened citing its fresh reply; never close while a supplier is untouched or a reply is in flight.
6. **Closing:** accept at our next goal (one extra round if it still moves > 0.5 %); after a final offer push 2 × 1 %
   **only when a rival's offer backs us up**; mirror an alternative sheet back before accepting it; close
   `max(90 s, slowest round + 15 s)` before a wave cap; never above the supplier's own price, never a broken must-have.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `engine.py` | `Config` (every tactic is a field), `Negotiator` (`goal`, `meso`, `write`, `run`, `run_rfq`, guards), `play()` |
| `target.py` | target C and price-for-C solver |
| `practice.py` | practice/final adapter: facts and floors from the data package |
| `variants.py` | named algorithms (A, A2, **A3**, B–H) and a parallel runner (max 4 sessions: the key's 10 are shared) |
| `search.py`, `report.py` | evolutionary tactic search on the sandbox and its report |
| `practice_report.py`, `summarize.py`, `cleanup.py`, `chat.py` | practice report, run summaries, safe cleanup, manual play |

Logs go to `proto/runs/` (git-ignored). `report.py` / `practice_report.py` write notes into `$VAULT_DIR` (default `../vault`).

"""Research-driven buyer prototype: code picks every number, templates write the e-mail.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D01 case:D02            # default Config
    ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2, "T": 4}' PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D02

Per round: target C (proto.target) -> concession curve on C -> equal-C term sheets (MESO) ->
templated e-mail (facts, answers, rival offer, question) -> replies -> acceptance rule.
Every tactic is a field of Config, so proto/search.py can try many variants in parallel.

import base64
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost
from arena_kit.cli import load_env
from arena_kit.cost import supplier_value
from arena_kit.docs import read_document, standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import ENDED

from proto.target import lever_grid, price_for_c, target

LOG_DIR = Path("proto/runs")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:

def run_one(client, name, cfg, case, rep, practice):
    if practice:
        from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
        eng.Negotiator = PracticeNegotiator
    for attempt in range(6):
        try:
            sid, res = eng.play(case, cfg, client=client, log_dir=OUT / name, quiet=True)
            break
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. 429 too many open sessions: wait for a slot
            time.sleep(10 * (attempt + 1))
    else:
        sid, res = None, {"score": None, "error": "could not open a session"}
    row = {"variant": name, "case": case, "rep": rep, "session": sid, "cfg": asdict(cfg), "score": res.get("score"),
           "c_deal": res.get("c_deal"), "c_best": res.get("c_best"), "terms": res.get("terms"), "error": res.get("error")}
    with open(OUT / "results.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--cases", nargs="+", default=["case:D01:1", "case:D02:3"])
    ap.add_argument("--variants", nargs="+", default=list(VARIANTS))
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--practice", action="store_true", help="data-package facts/floors (costs practice quota!)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    load_env()
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = ArenaClient()
    jobs = []
    for spec in a.cases:
        case, _, n = spec.rpartition(":") if spec.count(":") == 2 else (spec, None, "1")
        for rep in range(int(n)):
            for v in a.variants:
                jobs.append((v, VARIANTS[v][1], case, rep))
    print(f"{len(jobs)} sessions, {a.workers} at a time", flush=True)
    rows = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(a.workers) as ex:
        futs = [ex.submit(run_one, client, v, cfg, case, rep, a.practice) for v, cfg, case, rep in jobs]
        for i, f in enumerate(as_completed(futs), 1):
            r = f.result()
            rows.append(r)
            print(f"  [{i}/{len(jobs)}] {r['variant']} {r['case']} rep{r['rep']} score={r['score']} err={r['error']}", flush=True)
    table = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for r in rows:
        table[r["variant"]][r["case"]].append(r["score"] if r["score"] is not None else 0.0)
    cases = sorted({r["case"] for r in rows})
    print("\nvariant | " + " | ".join(cases))
    for v in a.variants:
        cells = []
        for c in cases:
            s = table[v][c]
            cells.append(f"{sum(s) / len(s):.3f} {[round(x, 3) for x in s]}" if s else "-")
        print(f"{v} {VARIANTS[v][0]} | " + " | ".join(cells))


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""The Live Final with Tugra's engine: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py                                   # Live Final: start before wave 1
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py --rehearse case:D01 case:D02      # free dress rehearsal (sandbox)
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py --rehearse case:D01 case:D02 -n 2 --cap 240   # tight cap, 4 sessions

Every case is played with algorithm A3 (proto/variants.py) through the data-package adapter (proto/practice.py:
facts and floors from the data, the Sunday release included). ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2}' overrides single settings.
What it keeps from the rules: one session per case (after a restart it resumes ours), at most 10 open sessions,
the wave's cap followed from `seconds_left` on every poll (the host may extend a wave), and it never reads
/v1/events, /screen, /leaderboard or /results. A broken case never stops the others or the runner.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import asdict, replace
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

import proto.engine as eng
from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
from proto.variants import VARIANTS

LOG = Path("proto/runs/final")
POLL_S = 5.0
_write = threading.Lock()


def config():
    """A3, with single settings overridden by ENGINE_CFG (JSON)."""
    return replace(VARIANTS["A3"][1], **json.loads(os.environ.get("ENGINE_CFG", "{}")))


def say(text):
    print(f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {text}", flush=True)


def one(client, case, cfg, deadline, log_dir):
    """Play one case to its end. Returns a result row; never raises."""
    cid, t0 = case["case_id"], time.time()
    row = {"case": cid, "wave": case.get("wave"), "theme": case.get("theme"), "started": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}
    try:
        sid, res = eng.play(cid, cfg, client=client, log_dir=log_dir, quiet=True, deadline=deadline, case=case)
        keep = ("deal", "score", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "c_alt", "end_reason", "supplier_id", "error")
        row.update(session=sid, **{k: res.get(k) for k in keep if k in res})
    except Exception as e:  # e.g. the session could not be opened at all
        row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
    cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline
    row.update(seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1), left_at_close=round(cap - time.time(), 1) if cap else None)
    with _write, open(LOG / "results.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, default=str) + "\n")
    score = row.get("score")
    say(f"{cid} (wave {row['wave']}): {'deal' if row.get('deal') else 'no deal'}, score {score}, "
        f"{row['seconds']} s, {row['left_at_close']} s before the cap {row.get('error') or ''}")
    return row


def summary(rows):
    waves = {}
    for r in rows:
        waves.setdefault(r.get("wave"), []).append(r.get("score") or 0.0)
    for w, s in sorted(waves.items(), key=lambda kv: str(kv[0])):
        deals = sum(bool(r.get("deal")) for r in rows if r.get("wave") == w)
        say(f"wave {w}: {len(s)} cases, {deals} deals, {100 * statistics.mean(s):.1f} points (our own record)")


def final(cfg, waves=5, parallel=10):
    """The Live Final: poll the case list, start every case of a running wave at once, follow each wave's cap."""
    client = ArenaClient()
    started, caps, closed = {}, {}, set()
    say(f"final runner up: A3 {asdict(cfg)}; waiting for wave 1 (polling every {POLL_S:.0f} s)")
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
        while len(closed) < waves or not all(f.done() for f in started.values()):
            try:
                try:
                    cases = client.cases("final")
                except ArenaError as e:
                    if e.status != 403:  # 403: no wave has started yet
                        raise
                    cases = []
                for case in cases:
                    w = case.get("wave")
                    if not case.get("open"):
                        if w not in closed:
                            say(f"wave {w} closed")
                        closed.add(w)
                        continue
                    if case.get("seconds_left") is not None:  # every poll: the host may extend a wave
                        caps[w] = time.time() + case["seconds_left"]
                    if case["case_id"] not in started:
                        if not any(c.get("wave") == w for c in cases if c["case_id"] in started):
                            say(f"wave {w} started: {case.get('theme')} ({case.get('seconds_left')} s)")
                        deadline = lambda w=w: caps.get(w)  # noqa: E731 - read at every decision
                        started[case["case_id"]] = pool.submit(one, client, case, cfg, deadline, LOG / f"wave{w}")
            except Exception as e:  # network trouble, a 5xx: keep polling, never die
                say(f"poll failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); retrying")
            time.sleep(POLL_S)
    rows = [f.result() for f in started.values()]
    summary(rows)
    return rows


def rehearse(case_ids, cfg, cap_s, repeats, practice_ok):
    """A dress rehearsal: the given cases as one wave, all at once, with a cap `cap_s` seconds from now."""
    client = ArenaClient()
    sets = {"sandbox": [], "practice": []}
    for cid in case_ids:
        sets["practice" if cid.startswith("case:P") else "sandbox"].append(cid)
    if sets["practice"] and not practice_ok:
        sys.exit("practice cases cost the team's quota: add --practice once the team has agreed")
    files = {c["case_id"]: c for s, ids in sets.items() if ids for c in client.cases(s)}
    jobs = [{**files[cid], "wave": "rehearsal", "theme": f"rehearsal {cap_s} s"} for cid in case_ids] * repeats
    if len(jobs) > 10:
        sys.exit("at most 10 sessions at once (the key's limit)")
    cap = time.time() + cap_s
    say(f"rehearsal: {len(jobs)} sessions at once, cap in {cap_s} s, A3 {asdict(cfg)}")
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs)) as pool:
        rows = list(pool.map(lambda c: one(client, c, cfg, lambda: cap, LOG / "rehearsal"), jobs))
    summary(rows)
    late = [r for r in rows if (r.get("left_at_close") or 0) < 0]
    say(f"closed after the cap: {len(late)} of {len(rows)}")
    return rows


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--rehearse", nargs="+", metavar="CASE", help="play these cases as one wave instead")
    ap.add_argument("--cap", type=int, default=480, help="rehearsal: the wave's cap in seconds (final: 480)")
    ap.add_argument("-n", "--repeats", type=int, default=1, help="rehearsal: sessions per case")
    ap.add_argument("--practice", action="store_true", help="rehearsal on practice cases (costs quota: ask first)")
    ap.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=10)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    load_env()
    LOG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    eng.Negotiator = PracticeNegotiator  # facts and floors from the data package, as for any unseen case
    cfg = config()
    if a.rehearse:
        rehearse(a.rehearse, cfg, a.cap, a.repeats, a.practice)
    else:
        final(cfg, a.waves, min(a.parallel, 10))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Sandbox results: Tugra's engine (branch `tugra`), A3 → A4, 2026-10-10 evening

All runs on the free hosted sandbox (D01 price increase, 1 supplier, `stabilise`; D02 RFQ, 2 suppliers, `leverage`).
No practice sessions used. Changes are in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tugra`, **not committed yet**.

## Headline

| Config | How it plays | D01 | D02 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 (Tugra's main) | hand-written sandbox facts | 0.979 | 0.740 | 0.860 |
| A3 | **data adapter = how the Live Final plays every case** | 0.894 (0.889, 0.905, 0.889) | 0.613 (0.640, 0.619, 0.492, 0.701) | 0.754 |
| **A4 (new)** | **data adapter** | **0.987** (0.969–0.996, 7 plays) | **0.684** (0.661–0.703, 10 plays) | **0.836** |

**A4 recovers most of what the hand-written facts were worth (+0.08 mean over A3 in the final's code path), with no
case-specific knowledge,** and its D02 is much steadier: 0.66–0.70 vs A3's 0.49–0.70.

## What changed (all on branch `tugra`)

1. **A4 = A3 + two settings that only act where our data knows nothing** (new suppliers or parts, the sandbox):
   - `game_evidence`: the supplier's floor from what it told us: the cost drivers it cites in its letter, its
     cost breakdown (after round 1), its material share. Before, the adapter fell back to "85 % of the lowest
     opening".
   - `blind_refs`: the case's own refs (`cost:`, `po:`, `fc:`, `sc:`, `news:`, a cheaper alternative quote) cited
     by ID with no figure of ours; the arena checks the ID against its own data. Before, the adapter cited nothing
     on an unknown supplier.
   - On all 10 hosted practice cases the data has the evidence, so **A4 plays exactly like A3 there** (checked
     offline): no risk to the practice results.
2. **`proto/final.py`, the Live Final runner** (there was none for this engine):
   - polls the waves and plays every case of a running wave in parallel, A4 through the data adapter;
   - follows the wave's cap on every poll (the host may extend a wave);
   - waits for a free session slot instead of losing the case;
   - never reads /events, /screen, /leaderboard or /results;
   - `--rehearse` for free dress rehearsals.
3. **Engine robustness**:
   - after a restart, the engine resumes our running final session instead of losing the case;
   - a crash takes the best offer that beats our alternative instead of walking away;
   - the cap is read live.
4. Tests: 4 new (wave loop, cap extension, a broken case, a full key, resume); 35 pass.

## Final-runner rehearsals (A4, cases started at once like a wave)

| Rehearsal | Plays | Result | Time left at close |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8-min cap | D01 ×2, D02 ×2 | 0.990, 0.996, 0.682, 0.682 · 4/4 deals | 338–436 s |
| 8-min cap, uncached | D01, D02 ×3 | 0.991, 0.682, 0.682, 0.703 · 4/4 deals | 270–386 s |
| **150-s cap**, uncached (stress) | D01, D02 | 0.977, 0.661 · 2/2 deals | 82 s, 53 s |

Closed after the cap: **0 of 12**.

## Caveats
- **The sandbox caches supplier replies to identical e-mails.** A deterministic engine sends the same e-mails every
  time, so repeats can be echoes (replies in 0.1 s), not new samples. Several "0.740 ×3" / "0.682 ×3" runs above
  are partly that. `--fresh` (a reference number in the subject) gives independent repeats; those are marked
  "uncached".
- 2 sandbox plays were lost to `429: at most 10 open sessions per key` while teammates also played. The runner now
  waits for a slot instead.
- Remaining gap on D02 vs the hand-written facts: 0.684 vs 0.740. The hand-written version knows the suppliers' cash
  needs and that the news "points to easing bar costs". The next sandbox ideas: cash-need cues from the supplier's
  own words, and reading the news direction.

## Decision needed: practice (costs team quota, 149 left)
- **4 weak cases** (P08, P10, P11, P18) through the final runner: 4 sessions. Pre-flight plus Tugra's planned
  retest; our board sits at 0.39–0.71 on those.

**What I changed on Tugra's engine:** the version you'll see as **A4** is Tugra's A3 plus two settings that only switch on when our data package knows nothing about a supplier or part.
- It reads the supplier's own evidence: the cost drivers it cites, its cost breakdown, its material share.

On the 10 hosted practice cases our data already has that evidence, so A4 plays exactly like A3 there.

**The finding that matters:** A3's sandbox scores rely on hand-written facts about the sandbox suppliers. The Live Final plays every case through the data-package path instead, so I tested both versions that way:

| Played as in the final | D01 | D02 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|

| **A4** | **0.987** | **0.684** (spread 0.66–0.70) | **0.836** |

A4 gains about 0.08 over A3 and its D02 results vary much less.

**Live Final runner:** there was none for this engine, so I added one (`proto/final.py`).
- It follows each wave's deadline, waits for a free session slot instead of losing a case, and picks up its own sessions again after a restart.
- A crash now accepts the best offer that beats our alternative instead of walking away.
- In 12 rehearsal sessions on the sandbox, all reached a deal and none closed after the cap, including under a deliberately short 150-second cap.

**One thing to know before reading older numbers:** the sandbox reuses supplier replies when it receives the exact same e-mails. Our engine always writes the same e-mails, so repeated runs can be echoes of an earlier run rather than new samples. That includes some of Tugra's "same score three times" runs and some of mine. The rehearsal tool now has a `--fresh` option that makes every e-mail unique, and the report marks which runs were fresh.

The changes are in the `tugra` worktree at `.claude/worktrees/tugra`; all 35 tests pass.

**Your decision on practice (149 sessions left):**
- **4 weak cases** (P08, P10, P11, P18): 4 sessions. This tests the final runner on real suppliers and retests the cases where our best is only 0.39–0.71. I'd go with this one.
- **1 case**: 1 session, just to check the final setup works.
- **All 10 hosted cases**: 10 sessions.

- **Replay:** [e843da929222686e](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e843da929222686e) (D02, **0.661**: J1 €14.10 FCA, 14 d, 35 d). Ours: A 0.640 (3/3), A2 0.626 (mean of 3), best single search run 0.724.
- **What the friend does differently:**
  1. **Staggered RFQ opening.** Messages only C1 (cheapest quote) first. C1 answers with a €15.50 alternative. We message both at once in round 0 with no rival info, and J1 reaches only €15.00–15.40 there.
  2. **Breakdown argument in the body:** "Your attached cost breakdown shows €5.56 material, €4.39 labour and €2.81 conversion, or €12.76 direct cost. A 24-month award with quick payment supports a positive margin at our proposed price." J1: "You are right about the direct costs…" → €14.60 → €14.10.
  3. **Volume framing for the supplier's motives:** "planning baseline 500 per month", "predictable 500-unit monthly orders", "a 42-day lead avoids overtime", "if a larger binding lot would change the price, quote the exact trade-off".
  4. Also: LLM-written, persona-tailored text; no push after J1's final offer.
- **Implemented as switches** (`Config.rfq_stagger`, `breakdown_arg`, `volume_framing`); variants **F** = A2 + stagger, **G** = A2 + breakdown + framing, **H** = A2 + all three.
- **Test:** D02 × 3 for F, G, H; D01 × 1 for G, H (F only changes RFQs).
- **Run 1:** F 0.746 / 0.724 / **0.374**; G 0.682 / 0.640 / 0.664 (D01 0.969); H 0.745 / **0.374** / 0.746 (D01 0.957).
- **Bug in the stagger (the two 0.374 runs):** J1 was **never contacted**. C1 (the lead) answered in < 1 s per round; J1's worker waited for "the lead's reply" but kept seeing the lead's *next* message in flight, so it waited its full 40 s while C1 negotiated 4 rounds alone and the case closed on C1 at €15.80. **Fix:** the others wait only for the lead's *first* reply; the lead pauses after round 0 until every supplier has its first message; and the engine never closes while a supplier is still untouched (`untouched` in `hold_close`).
- **Run 2 (fixed):** **F 0.740 / 0.740 / 0.703 (mean 0.728)**, H 0.745 / 0.724 / 0.703 (0.724). No outliers.

# Practice run A5 (all 10 hosted cases): every result and every problem

Algorithm A5 on the generic code path (what the final runs). 10 practice sessions (quota 140 → 130), 2026-10-10 evening, arena under heavy load (supplier replies up to ~113 s). Raw table with replays: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A5]]. Full transcripts: `starter-kit/proto/runs/variants/A5/` (extract with `proto/inspect_run.py A5`).

## Results

| Case | Type · goal | **A5** | Best before | Teammate | Record | Deal | C_deal vs C_best | Rounds / s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| **P05** | RFQ, 3 suppliers · leverage | **0.000** ❌ | 0.614 | 0.41 | 0.676 | **no deal**: two suppliers *agreed*, both lost (bug 1) | – | 4 / 214 |

| P10 | capacity · secure supply | 0.679 | 0.679 | 0.655 | 0.679 | €31.50, 36 mo, 23,400/yr, 56-day lead (final) | 1,522,963 vs 1,328,927 (+14.6 %) | 2 / 30 |

**Best per case over all our runs: 0.703** (P01 0.881, P02 0.684, P03 0.923, P04 0.874, P05 0.614, P07 0.710, P08 0.482, P10 0.679, P11 0.710, P18 0.286).

## Problems, most severe first

### 1. ❌ Critical: an agreed RFQ deal was lost while we waited (P05 = 0)
- **Evidence:** Dralveck (70210) **agreed** to our sheet at €29.27 (received at 161 s); Fuchsreiter (70250) agreed at €29.97 (193 s). The closing guard waited because a rival reply was in flight. We sent the accept at 207 s, and the arena answered: *"late: more than 60 s after the supplier's last move, so it counted as a timeout (your last offer, repeated)"*. The agreed sheet was no longer standing (`422 not a standing offer`). Our fallback then treated the session as ended and stopped, so **no deal**.
- **Why:** (a) under load the supplier's move happened well before we *received* it (replies took 48–113 s to arrive), so our "45 s of waiting" was really > 60 s on the arena's clock; (b) after a failed accept we gave up instead of re-reading the thread and accepting the new standing sheet.
- **Fix:** accept an `agreed` (or acceptable final) offer **at once**, never hold it for a rival; on a late/422 accept, **GET the thread and accept its current standing sheet**; never end our side of a live session after a failed close.

### 2. ❌ High: packages that were not equal in cost to us (P02)
- **Evidence:** round 2 sent €364.50 / 90 d (C 2,235,459 ≈ C_best) and €360.32 / 60 d + CU clause (C 2,256,842). The supplier agreed to the **clause package, €21k worse for us**.
- **Why:** "equal C" tolerance was 1 % of C (€22k), larger than the whole room of this case (2.1 % open → best).
- **Fix:** tolerance = min(0.2 % of C, 10 % of the room open → target).

### 3. ❌ High: an insisted term was dropped again (P18)
- **Evidence:** round 1 the supplier made the AS-14404 clause a condition; we met it (€5.53, clause, 90 d). Round 3 our packages had **no clause** again; the supplier hardened and went final at €5.70–5.80.
- **Why (bug):** the "never in our sheets" check rejected the term in round 3 *because we had offered it in round 2*.
- **Fix:** a term we have met stays met (skip that check for persisted terms).

### 4. ⚠️ Medium: we let a better earlier offer go (P18, P08)
- **Evidence:** P18 round 1 alternative €5.70 + clause (5 %) / 60 d had C 272,612; after our push the final offers were C 275,561–278,691. P08: round 3 we switched to 14-day payment / 36 months and ended at C 1,051,250 vs 1,050,224 standing a round earlier.
- **Fix:** track the best offer seen; when a supplier's offers get worse after our move and it is close to final, stop pushing and accept the best standing one.

### 5. ⚠️ Medium: requests for proof we never answered (P03, P04, P05, P08, P11)
- **Evidence:** *"Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data."* (P03, P08, P11), *"Please provide proof of this total requirement so we can verify it"* (P04), *"we would need some proof for these figures"* (P05).
- **Fix:** when a supplier asks for data or proof, **attach a short data sheet** with the facts we cited (IDs and the values from `facts.json`: forecast change, order prices, scorecard, should-cost).

### 6. ⚠️ Medium: our target is too timid where the room is big (P07, P08, P18, P10)
- **Evidence:** P07 target C 318,889 vs C_best 299,241 (our first ask was already 6 % above the best possible); P08 975,580 vs 960,309; P18 256,608 vs 222,651; P10 1,260,946 vs 1,328,927 (here too bold).
- **Why:** without a supplier breakdown or should-cost, the floor is "current price / (1 + margin) × drift", capped at the opening, which says little about real room.
- **Fix (to test):** use the supplier's stated material share ("Material accounts for about 61 %") and the material index move to bound the floor; keep the bottleneck rule for `secure_supply`.

### 7. ⚠️ Medium: "price frozen, talk about terms" was not used (P03)
- **Evidence:** *"Our management has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. We can talk about the terms instead – payment, volume or contract length."* We kept asking for price.
- **Fix (to test):** when a supplier freezes price, offer packages that change only terms (contract length, payment, volume) at its price.

### 8. Info: arena load
- Supplier replies took 1–113 s (P05). The 25-second re-fetch fix (E23) kept every other case inside its clocks, but P05 shows how tight the 60-second window gets in RFQs under load.

## Fix plan → A6
1. Accept agreed/final offers immediately; recover from late/422 accepts (problem 1).
2. Tight equal-C tolerance relative to the room (problem 2).
3. Persist met terms (problem 3).
4. Best-seen guard near the end (problem 4).
5. Proof/data attachment on request (problem 5).
6. Tested on the sandbox (free) and the offline smoke test of all 19 case files first; practice only after the team's OK.

# Exact D02 algorithm that reproducibly scored 0.661

Implementation: `EvidenceTraderAgent(d02_style="j1_cost", d02_target_cost=170638.57)` in
`starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/evidence.py`, ehl-tacto commit `4bf381e` on branch
`sudeep/negotiation-experiments`. The batch configuration is
`starter-kit/experiments/qualification.json`. This is a **deterministic, demo-specific state
machine**. It uses fixed bid templates and evidence IDs; there is no LLM, reinforcement learning,
or fitted opponent model in this policy.

## Inputs and invariant checks

- Read the D02 case plus both current supplier threads, including quote attachments and any
  alternative term sheets in the latest supplier reply.
- For each current supplier sheet, fill missing fields from that supplier's quote PDF/standard
  terms. Reject sheets whose resulting lead time exceeds **42 days**. This rejects C1's opening
  €16.00 quote because its omitted lead time defaults to **45 days**.
- Calculate **complete buyer cost** over 6,000 units/year for 24 months: purchases + payment
  financing + freight + lateness beyond 35 days + expected quality loss. Choose by this cost, not
  the lowest unit price. Only a current, valid supplier sheet can be accepted.
- If any valid standing sheet has cost **≤ €170,638.57**, accept the cheapest such sheet immediately.
  This threshold corresponds to the D02 score needed for the team's combined 0.8 gate given the
  repeated D01 score. No D02 sheet reached it in the recorded runs.

## Message state machine

Each supplier's state is the number of buyer emails already sent to that thread. All bid sheets
use **14-day payment**; the case fixes the contract at **24 months**. The email states the real
**6,000-unit annual requirement**; the agent never invents a larger commitment.

| Decision point | Supplier and exact structured bids (`€/unit`, Incoterm, lead days) | Evidence and purpose |

| C1 has 0 buyer emails | C1: `14.50 EXW 42`, `14.80 FCA 42`, `15.00 DAP 35` | Cite `fc:SH-220@2026-09`; get a valid competing quote while offering 14-day cash and flexible delivery. C1 replied with a valid **€15.50 EXW / 42-day** alternative. |

# D02: J1 evidence and cost-breakdown trade reached 0.661

**Official sandbox score:** 0.6608797298. **Deal:** Demo Drehteile GmbH (`sup:DEMO-J1`) at **€14.10/unit, 14-day payment, 35-day lead, FCA**, for the case's fixed 6,000 units/year and 24 months. The 42-day maximum lead-time must-have was met. Total buyer cost was **€176,257.60**, compared with opening cost €214,296.00, reference best cost €156,738.78, and the no-deal alternative €238,800.00. [Replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/6fe86ce06c0af781).

For the exact state machine, bid prices, references, stopping rule and reproduction command, see
[[D02-J1-Evidence-Trader-Algorithm]].

## The algorithm

This is a **deterministic, D02-specific evidence-and-package bargaining policy**, not reinforcement learning. It has fixed offer templates and a small state machine driven by how many messages have been sent to each supplier. The live supplier replies determine which *current* offer is best and which rival price can truthfully be cited.

1. **Value before acting.** Read both supplier threads, their quote attachments and all current main/alternative term sheets. Fill missing terms from each supplier's standard quote. Reject any offer with lead time above 42 days. For the rest, calculate complete two-year buyer cost: price for 12,000 units, financing, freight, lateness and expected quality cost. Rank by this cost, not quoted unit price. An invalid or superseded offer is never the fallback.
2. **Create a credible alternative at C1.** First send three packages with 14-day payment: €14.50 EXW/42-day lead, €14.80 FCA/42 days and €15.00 DAP/35 days. Cite the real forecast `fc:SH-220@2026-09` and keep annual volume at 6,000. This is meant to elicit a valid, comparable C1 quote; the opening C1 quote omits lead time and its standard 45 days violates the must-have.
3. **Use that alternative to bargain with J1.** Name C1's *actual current valid quote* and cite `news:N-0412`. Send three J1 packages, all with 14-day payment: €13.80 DAP/35 days, €13.40 EXW/42 days and €14.00 FCA/35 days. Do not invent a rival price. The cash and lead-time terms give J1 something of value while the distinct delivery packages reveal its tradeoffs.
4. **Make one evidence-backed J1 follow-up.** On J1's reply, cite `cost:part:SH-220` and `sc:DEMO-J1@2026Q3`. If its attachment actually contains the observed €5.56 material, €4.39 labour and €2.81 conversion figures, refer to that breakdown. Offer €13.40 EXW/42 days, €13.80 DAP/35 days and €13.60 FCA/35 days, all with 14-day payment. This was the move before J1's €14.10 FCA counter.
5. **Close by complete cost.** Continue comparing the latest valid sheets from both suppliers, including alternatives. If a sheet meets the target cost, accept it immediately. Otherwise contact the supplier with fewer buyer messages, with at most four messages to either thread; accept the cheapest currently executable sheet when the useful exchanges are exhausted or suppliers mark offers final/agreed. In this run J1's €14.10 FCA/35-day sheet beat its cheaper-looking €13.90 EXW/42-day alternative after freight and lateness, so the agent accepted J1's final offer.

For the six-run qualification batch, the early-accept target was **€170,638.57** (the D02 cost needed for a 0.8 combined score given D01 at 0.841495). The target was never reached, so the final-offer close rule selected J1. This is a demo-tuned policy; the prices, references and supplier ordering are not yet generalized to P-cases.

## Policy and sequence

This was the deterministic `EvidenceTraderAgent(d02_style="j1_cost")` in `starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/evidence.py` on the `sudeep/negotiation-experiments` branch. It compared *complete* offer cost and checked the hard lead-time limit before accepting. It used short fixed emails, no LLM or trained RL policy.

1. **Establish a real alternative with C1.** Offered three packages trading 14-day payment, delivery terms and lead time, citing `fc:SH-220@2026-09` for the actual 6,000-unit annual forecast. C1 verified the forecast and quoted **€15.50 EXW / 14 days / 42-day lead** as an alternative. C1's opening €16.00 had omitted lead time; its standard 45 days would have failed the must-have.
2. **Open J1 with the valid rival quote and a relevant news reference.** The message named C1's current €15.50 EXW / 14-day / 42-day quote and its offer ID, and cited `news:N-0412`. Three structured packages asked for €13.80 DAP/35 days, €13.40 EXW/42 days, or €14.00 FCA/35 days, all with 14-day payment. J1 reported both the rival-quote and news claims **verified**, then countered at **€14.60 FCA / 14 days / 35 days** (also €14.50 EXW / 42 days). This was the large step versus the earlier generic strategies.
3. **Use J1's own cost breakdown and scorecard.** Its attached breakdown showed €5.56 material + €4.39 labour + €2.81 conversion = €12.76 direct cost per unit, before overhead and profit. The next message cited `cost:part:SH-220` and `sc:DEMO-J1@2026Q3`, kept 14-day payment and the 24-month volume, and asked for alternative packages. J1 verified those two claims and moved to **€14.10 FCA / 14 days / 35 days**, with a €13.90 EXW / 42-day alternative. The FCA package had the lower *total* buyer cost despite its higher unit price: EXW added freight and a seven-day late-delivery charge.
4. **Compare the other supplier and close.** C1 would only reach €15.30 EXW / 42 days. A further price request to J1 drew a `final_offer` at €14.10 FCA; J1 said direct cost excluded overhead. The policy accepted J1's standing final offer. The case ended after eight buyer actions, including acceptance, with a deal and no protocol or must-have failure.

Cost of the accepted J1 offer: purchases €169,200; financing for 14-day payment €1,729.60; FCA freight €4,800; expected quality €528; no late-delivery charge. These sum to €176,257.60.

## Learning and next gate

Using a **specific, valid competing offer** plus `news:N-0412` coincided with a much better J1 first counter; the verified J1 delivery and should-cost references preceded another €0.50/unit reduction. A further lower-price request without new evidence produced a final-offer lock; J1 referred back to overhead in its reply. The agent should ask for an economically equivalent package or close rather than keep lowering its ask without a new trade.

This initial run alone was not a repeatability result. The original per-case **0.8 gate was not met**: with the observed `C_open` and `C_best`, score 0.8 requires a buyer cost at or below about **€168,250.22**, another **€8,007.38** below this deal. The team has not authorized spending the 200-session practice quota for this experiment; all runs here were on quota-free D01/D02 sandbox.

A separate `j1_soft` probe removed the repeated direct-cost argument in the later message, but it
closed on the same €14.10 FCA J1 offer and scored **0.6608797298**. This supports keeping the
earlier verified-evidence sequence; it does not prove that every wording variant behaves the same.

The team subsequently revised the decision gate: use at least three runs per case and require the
midpoint of the D01 and D02 **case medians** to reach 0.8. Given D01's repeated 0.841495 score, a
matching D02 strategy needs a repeated median of at least 0.758505.

The exact `j1_cost` policy was then run **three times on each demo**. All six sessions ended in a
deal. D01 was **0.841495 / €414,993.77** in each run; D02 was **0.660880 / €176,257.60** in each
run. The case-balanced combined median was **0.751187**, below the revised 0.8 gate. The repeated
D02 replays are [run 1](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e843da929222686e),
[run 2](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/a40f20f453858602), and
[run 3](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e38acad546436805). Identical replies from these demo bots
show repeatability here, not generalization to unseen suppliers. This strategy is therefore a
stepping stone, not a qualified winner.

Raw local artifacts: `ehl-tacto-experiments/logs/experiments/20261010T134745Z-0373e634/` (ignored by Git). The replay above is the portable record.

def goal(self, rnd):
        best = self.best_standing()
        ref = self.c_open if self.cfg.toward == "open" else (best[0] if best else self.c_open)
        ref = min(ref, self.c_alt)
        start = self.target_c * (1 + self.cfg.anchor)
        if self.cfg.bottleneck_anchor and self.b.get("category_goal") == "secure_supply" and self.c_open < float("inf"):
            # practice P10: 17 % below a bottleneck's opening -> "far below any calculation", final above opening
            start = max(start, self.c_open * (1 - self.cfg.bottleneck_anchor))
        if self.cfg.anchor_mode == "opening" and self.c_open < float("inf"):
            # teammates' rule: the first ask sits a goal-specific % below the opening, never below our target
            start = max(start, self.c_open * (1 - GOAL_ANCHOR.get(self.b.get("category_goal"), 0.10)))
        frac = min(1.0, max(rnd, 0) / self.cfg.T) ** (1 / self.cfg.e)
        return start + (ref - start) * frac

    def meso(self, t, c_goal):
        """Up to meso_n packages that each cost us c_goal, differing in the levers the supplier may value."""
        offered = t.sheets[0]["terms"] if t.sheets else {}
        grid = [g for g in lever_grid(self.case, {**t.std, **offered}) if must_haves_ok(self.case, g, t.std)]
        months = self.case.get("term_options", {}).get("contract_months")
        if self.cfg.long_contract and months and "contract_months" in self.case["negotiable"]:
            longest = max(months)  # beyond the horizon it costs nothing; suppliers value the security
            if longest >= 12 * self.b["horizon_years"]:
                grid = [g for g in grid if g.get("contract_months") == longest] or grid
        their_price = offered.get("unit_price")
        their_c = self.C(t, offered) if offered.get("unit_price") is not None else float("inf")
        priced = []
        for g in grid:
            p = price_for_c(self.case, g, t.std, c_goal, t.est if self.relationship else None)
            terms = complete_offer(self.case, {**g, "unit_price": p})
            c = self.C(t, terms)
            if p <= 0.5 or (abs(c - c_goal) > 0.01 * c_goal and c < c_goal):
                continue
            # guard (teammates' P02 zero): never offer a higher price than the supplier itself asks,
            # and never a package that costs us more than its standing offer
            if their_price is not None and (p > their_price or c >= their_c):
                continue
            near = sum(terms.get(k) != offered.get(k) for k in terms if k != "unit_price" and k in offered)
            priced.append((supplier_value(self.case, terms, t.est), near, terms, c))
        everything = list(priced)
        hits = [x for x in priced if abs(x[3] - c_goal) <= 0.01 * c_goal]
        if not hits and priced:
            # the goal is out of reach (e.g. below what the supplier-health term allows): offer the
            # packages closest to it, i.e. the cheapest ones for us, each at its cheapest price
            lowest = min(x[3] for x in priced)
            hits = [x for x in priced if x[3] <= lowest * 1.005]
        priced = [x[:3] for x in hits]
        if not priced:
            return []
        if self.cfg.pick == "near":
            priced.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], -x[0]))
        else:
            priced.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
        picks = [priced[0][2]]
        for _, _, terms in priced[1:]:
            if len(picks) >= self.cfg.meso_n:
                break
            if self.cfg.pick == "near" or all(sum(terms.get(k) != q.get(k) for k in terms if k != "unit_price") >= 2 for q in picks):
                picks.append(terms)
        for _, _, terms in priced[1:]:
            if len(picks) >= self.cfg.meso_n:
                break
            if terms not in picks:
                picks.append(terms)
        if self.cfg.meet_fields and offered:
            # practice P08/P18: the supplier insisted on its index clause and we never offered one back
            ours = [s2["terms"] for m in t.events if m.get("from") == "buyer" for s2 in m.get("term_sheets") or []]
            theirs = [(m.get("term_sheets") or [{}])[0].get("terms", {}) for m in t.events if m.get("from") not in ("buyer", "arena")]
            order = sorted((f for f in self.case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"), key=lambda f: f != "index_clause")
            for f in order:  # at most one met field per message, the index clause first
                if f not in offered or offered[f] is None or any(q.get(f) == offered[f] for q in picks):
                    continue
                # only a term the supplier introduced itself (never in our sheets) and kept in its last two offers,
                # after it has seen at least one of ours - not an echo of our own packages (sandbox D01)
                if not ours or any(o.get(f) == offered[f] for o in ours) or len(theirs) < 2 \
                        or any(x.get(f) != offered[f] for x in theirs[-2:]):
                    continue
                cands = [x for x in everything if x[2].get(f) == offered[f]
                         and (their_price is None or x[2]["unit_price"] >= 0.85 * their_price)]  # no absurd asks
                if cands:
                    best = min(cands, key=lambda x: abs(x[3] - c_goal))[2]
                    if len(picks) >= self.cfg.meso_n:
                        picks[-1] = best
                    else:
                        picks.append(best)
                    self.note("meet_field", supplier=t.sid, field=f, value=offered[f], price=best["unit_price"])
                    break
        return picks

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`
## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.
